page.layout: One page of text, one column, with a heading-free running head at top; a marginal-free block of text; at the foot a printed woodcut ornament and a small asterisk ornament, no text beside them.

p.i: equos ducunt, vt cum Currus velocitate a-gatur, firmè tamen & inconcusse procedat.

main_text.p: Acrimonia & Virilitas subsequen-tes duos moderantur equos, ut viriliter & cum acrimonia Currus incedere possit.
Ante illos equos duo alii incedunt, qui semper progredi conantur, & per Magnanimitatem & Audaciam gubernan-tur.

Verùm ne Magnanimitas & Audacia Currum per avia rapiant, ante illos duos equos alii duo incedunt, qui per Experientiam & Solertiam reguntur: quoniam nisi Experientia & Solertia inhibe-ant, facilitêr Magnanimitas & Audacia Currum evertere pos-sent.

page.notes: Woodcut ornament and asterisk ornament at the foot are not text and are not transcribed. The running head and page number are read from the top of the scan. Possible printing irregularities: "facilitêr" is read with a circumflex-like mark on the e, which is uncertain; marked as printed. The word "inconcusse" and the final line "sent." are the continuation of "possent"; the broken word "pos-sent" is kept with its printed hyphen. Heading "Virilitas" etc. are plain text, not headings.
